title: Yashigani MCP OPA Input Schema
description: Input document schema for the mcp.rego policy package. Describes the structure of input passed by the gateway when evaluating MCP-posture requests and their responses.

posture.description: MCP deployment posture. mcp-a: local stdio Shape A, mcp-b: remote Streamable-HTTP Shape B, mcp-c: multi-hop chained Shape C.

action.description: The MCP action being requested. Use dot-notation: mcp.prompts.list, mcp.tools.call, mcp.resources.read, etc.

identity.description: Resolved caller identity, populated by the gateway from the SPIFFE certificate or JWT.

spiffe.description: SPIFFE URI of the immediate caller, e.g. spiffe://cluster.local/ns/default/sa/langflow. Empty string when SPIFFE is not present (treated as anonymous in policy).

verified.description: v4.1 Phase 2a/2b (LU-MCP-A1): true ONLY when the transport layer verified the caller's per-instance leaf certificate at TLS (SPIFFE URI SAN + trust chain — never hostname; instance-leaf SANs are loopback-only). MUST be set by the transport layer, never from the request body. false = identity.spiffe is a broker assertion built from context fields. Policy requires verified == true (strict boolean) on all mcp-b/mcp-c allow paths (yashigani.mcp _identity_verified rule); a broker-asserted, name-derived SPIFFE alone no longer authorizes. The producer always emits this field; absence is treated as false (fail-closed).

chain.description: Full upstream identity chain for multi-hop MCP-C calls. Each entry is a SPIFFE URI representing a hop in call-order (index 0 = originating caller, last = immediate caller). Populated by the MCP-C JWT (P2/N3 chunk). Absent on mcp-a and mcp-b. Policy enforces max depth via mcp_chain_max_depth.

items.description: SPIFFE URI of a hop in the chain.

tool.description: Present when action is mcp.tools.call. Mutually exclusive with prompt and resource (oneOf enforced by policy). Must NOT be present together with prompt or resource.

name.description: Tool name as declared in the MCP server manifest's tools list.

args.description: FIX-P3-001: full (non-redacted) tool-call arguments with path-bearing values NFKC-normalised and iteratively percent-decoded by the broker before OPA evaluation. The policy (and per-agent layers — filesystem/git path guards) applies literal '../' and startswith('/') checks against these already-decoded strings (encoded-traversal prevention). Kept in lock-step with _build_opa_input().

args_redacted.description: Tool call arguments with all secret-like values redacted to '<REDACTED>'. The gateway must perform redaction before populating this field. The policy uses this field for audit capture only — never for allow/deny decisions on argument values.

prompt.description: Present when action is mcp.prompts.list or mcp.prompts.get. Mutually exclusive with tool and resource (oneOf enforced by policy).

name.description: Prompt name as declared in the MCP server manifest.

sensitivity.description: Sensitivity label of the prompt content. Absent when not classified — policy treats absent as PUBLIC (conservative for prompt listing, caller-ceiling-checked for prompt content).

resource.description: Present when action is mcp.resources.read or mcp.resources.list. Mutually exclusive with tool and prompt (oneOf enforced by policy).

uri.description: Resource URI as declared in the MCP server manifest, e.g. file:///data/reports or https://internal.example.com/docs/api.

sensitivity.description: Sensitivity label of the resource content. Absent when not classified — policy treats absent as PUBLIC.

target.description: v4.1 Phase 2a/2b (LU-MCP-A2/A3, lu.md §3a): the per-instance MCP target of this request, populated by the gateway/broker from the transport layer and call context. Emitted whenever the stable per-instance mcp_id is known; REQUIRED (by policy) for mcp.tools.call on mcp-b/mcp-c — policy denies invocation without target.mcp_id (instance_unidentified) and without a surface_hash matching the approved baseline (capability_envelope_drift / capability_envelope_not_active). Keys into data.yashigani.mcp.grants[mcp_id] and data.yashigani.mcp.baselines[mcp_id].

mcp_id.description: Stable per-instance MCP UUID minted once at first registration (ctx.mcp_id / McpIdStore / McpBrokerServerConfig.mcp_id). Two same-named MCPs in one tenant share a name-SPIFFE but never an mcp_id — this field is what lets OPA enforce per-instance grants.

cert_fingerprint.description: SHA-256 fingerprint of the per-instance leaf certificate presented at TLS, formatted 'sha256:<lowercase hex, no separators>' (broker-normalised). Binds the OPA decision log / audit record to the presenting instance's cert material.

surface_hash.description: 'sha256:<hex>' hash of the tool surface advertised by the instance at call time (yashigani.mcp._envelope.surface_set_hash — RFC-8785-style canonicalised byte-hash, broker-normalised with the sha256: prefix). Compared by policy against data.yashigani.mcp.baselines[mcp_id].surface_hash for change-prevention.

caller.description: 3.1 Phase 1 caller identity context (agent_id / user_id), passed from McpCallContext. Purely additive — policies that do not reference input.caller ignore it. Documented here to keep the schema in lock-step with _build_opa_input(). NOTE: the mcp_response_decision input (a DIFFERENT document, built by query_mcp_response_decision) also uses a top-level 'caller' object with {spiffe, sensitivity_ceiling, groups} — see the egress property below and policy/mcp.rego G-ORCH-OPA-1 header.

egress.description: v4.1 unified-sidecar Phase 1 (Lu M1 / Laura L-US-1) — FIRST-CLASS egress context on the mcp_response_decision input document (NOT on mcp_decision). Emitted by query_mcp_response_decision(egress_prefix=...) for EVERY /egress/eval request; never emitted on the broker tool-result path. Policy semantics key on the PRESENCE of this key: when present, allow additionally requires input.egress.prefix ∈ data.yashigani.mcp.egress_grants[input.caller.spiffe].prefixes with a tenant-scope conjunct (closed world — absent/empty grant data, ungranted prefix, wrong-instance SPIFFE, tenant mismatch all deny with caller_not_granted_prefix / MCP_EGRESS_PREFIX_NOT_GRANTED). Crafted null/false/{} values still count as present (fail-closed). The prefix is never smuggled inside tool.name for decisioning — tool.name 'egress:<prefix>' stays audit context only. Documented here to keep the schema in lock-step with the producer.

prefix.description: Egress destination prefix slug from /egress/eval/{prefix}/{path} (e.g. slack, slack-hooks, telegram, llm). Grant-set membership is exact string equality.

agent.description: Agent context. Present when the caller is a registered Yashigani agent.

runtime.description: Agent runtime identifier, e.g. langflow, n8n, openai-assistant, custom. Used by policy for posture-specific enforcement.

name.description: FIX-P3-ENFORCE / Iris F2: agent (MCP server) name, emitted by _build_opa_input() so per-agent rego packages (e.g. yashigani.agents.filesystem) can inspect it. Documented here to keep the schema in lock-step with the producer.

budget.description: Budget context for cost-aware gating. All fields optional — absent budget fields are treated as unconstrained (allow). Operators who configure budgets populate this field via the gateway budget enforcer.

this_call_estimate.description: Estimated cost of this call in abstract token-equivalent units. null means unknown/unconstrained. Policy uses this for rate_limit_key selection but does NOT block on cost (budget blocking is handled by the gateway budget enforcer upstream of OPA).

allOf.description: tool, prompt, resource are mutually exclusive. Exactly zero or one may be present. (At least one SHOULD be present for tool/prompt/resource actions, but the policy does not require it at the schema level — absence of all three results in deny.)

$comment: Decision return shape (not validated here — returned by OPA, not sent to OPA): { allow: bool, redact_args: [string], audit_capture: bool, rate_limit_key: string | null }

mcp_decision.title: MCP OPA Decision Shape
mcp_decision.description: Shape returned by OPA at /v1/data/yashigani/mcp/mcp_decision. NOT an input field — documented here for gateway implementers.

deny_reason.description: Human-readable reason for the deny decision. Value is 'ok' when allow is true. Values: ok, missing_spiffe_identity, invalid_posture, chain_depth_exceeded, multiple_subjects_in_request, missing_subject, unrecognised_action, tool_not_in_exposed_allowlist, mcp_c_requires_chain, spiffe_not_verified, tool_subject_required, instance_unidentified, capability_envelope_not_active, no_per_instance_grant, capability_envelope_drift (the last six added in v4.1 Phase 2b per-instance authz — LU-MCP-A1..A4).

redact_args.description: List of tool argument keys that must be redacted before logging. Empty when tool is not present.

audit_capture.description: Whether the gateway must write a full audit record (including redacted args) for this call.

rate_limit_key.description: Rate-limit bucket key for this call, e.g. spiffe + action + tool name. null means no rate limiting required.
